title: Christ the Head of the Church
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
searchTerms: Christ the Head of the Church
definition: Christ the Head of the Church means that Jesus alone has supreme authority over His people. The church belongs to Him and must submit to His Word, His rule, His mission, and His care.
summary: Christ the Head of the Church means that Jesus alone has supreme authority over His people. The church belongs to Him and must submit to His Word, His rule, His mission, and His care.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is not merely honored by the church; He rules the church. He is the risen Lord who nourishes, leads, corrects, protects, and builds His body according to His will.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The church does not belong to pastors, leaders, traditions, denominations, personalities, donors, culture, or the preferences of the people. Christ is the Head of the Church. He has first place in everything.

Because Christ is Head, the church must submit to His Word. Human leadership is real and necessary, but it is always servant leadership under Christ. No leader has authority to rule the church apart from the truth and character of Jesus.

Christ’s headship is not harsh or distant. He loves the church, gave Himself for her, sanctifies her, nourishes her, and prepares her for glory.

This doctrine also protects the church from being shaped by pride, fear, entertainment, politics, greed, or personality-driven ministry. The church is healthiest when Christ is central, Scripture is obeyed, leaders serve humbly, and the body follows the Lord together.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
When Christ’s headship is forgotten, churches become vulnerable to control, manipulation, celebrity culture, compromise, and spiritual abuse. People may begin serving human agendas while still using Christian language.

This doctrine brings the church back to safety and truth. Christ is strong enough to lead His people, loving enough to care for them, holy enough to correct them, and faithful enough to keep building His church even through weakness and opposition.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Submit your view of the church to Christ. Do not follow leaders, traditions, trends, or preferences above Him. Pray for church leaders to shepherd under Christ faithfully, and examine your own heart so your service, worship, correction, and ministry are done under His lordship and for His glory.
